description: A cat owner must decide whether to arrange a long-weekend pet-sitting exchange with a neighbor and finalize the exact care, meal compensation, medication, and key-handoff terms after a kitchen-table check-in with the people involved.

shared_context.S1: Mara needs someone to care for her cat over the long weekend from Friday evening through Monday morning.
shared_context.S2: Mara will make the final call about the arrangement and its terms.
shared_context.S3: Several people at the kitchen-table check-in have discussed helping with the cat.
shared_context.S4: For weekend arrangements, people in the household normally discuss availability, costs, care instructions, and access details at the kitchen table before making plans.
shared_context.S5: Mara has set aside Friday afternoon to review the cat's care plan and key handoff with the people involved before leaving.
shared_context.S6: At this check-in, the household's normal procedure is for each person to state their exact offer or requirement directly, while Mara records who supplied each item; Mara does not finalize the arrangement until every person has had that opportunity and she has read back the recorded items for confirmation.

PF1.text: Eli can care for the cat from Friday at 18:00 until Monday at 08:00 and will do it in exchange for exactly three homemade freezer meals from Mara.

PF2.text: Tessa can provide paid care for the same Friday 18:00 to Monday 08:00 window for exactly $120, an alternative she has not yet mentioned to Mara.

PF3.text: The cat's veterinary clinic told Jon that the cat's medicine must be given at exactly 08:00 and 20:00, with food, during the weekend; Jon has not yet shared this instruction with Mara.

PF4.text: The building manager told Rina that unattended keys and lockboxes are not allowed, so the apartment key must be handed to the sitter in person by Friday at 17:00; Rina has not yet told Mara.

acceptance_conditions: Eli must be selected as the caregiver.
The care window must cover exactly Friday 18:00 through Monday 08:00.
Mara must provide exactly three homemade freezer meals as compensation.
The $120 paid-care alternative must be recorded and credited for comparison.
The cat's medicine must be scheduled at exactly 08:00 and 20:00 with food.
The key must be handed to the sitter in person by Friday at 17:00.
The settlement must include explicit meal-exchange, medication-care, and in-person-key-handoff commitments.
The final justification must cite PF1, PF2, PF3, and PF4.

content_checks.C4: decisions['medication_morning_time'] == '08:00' and decisions['medication_evening_time'] == '20:00' and decisions['medication_with_food'] == True
content_checks.C5: any(c['type'] == 'key_handoff' and 'in person' in c['detail'] and 'Friday' in c['detail'] and '17:00' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] in ['compensation', 'compensation_commitment', 'meal_exchange', 'meal-exchange'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: decisions['care_window'] in ['Friday 18:00 to Monday 08:00', 'Friday 18:00 through Monday 08:00', 'Friday 18:00-Monday 08:00', 'Friday 18:00 - Monday 08:00']
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] in ['medication', 'medication_compliance', 'medication-care', 'care_instruction', 'caregiver_assignment', 'caregiver_commitment', 'care_plan_review', 'care_plan_review_commitment', 'medication_review'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: decisions['key_handoff_by'] == 'Friday' and decisions['key_handoff_time'] == '17:00' and decisions['key_handoff_method'] == 'in person'

decisive_facts.why: Eli's exact offer selects him, fixes compensation at exactly three freezer meals, requires a meal-exchange commitment, and fixes the care window at Friday 18:00 through Monday 08:00.
Tessa's exact alternative changes the comparison record from no concrete paid benchmark to exactly $120 and requires PF2 to be credited.
The clinic instruction changes medication from an unspecified routine to exactly 08:00 and 20:00 with food and requires an explicit medication-care or care-instruction commitment.

The building rule changes key access from an unspecified arrangement to an in-person handoff by exactly Friday at 17:00 and requires both exact decision fields and an explicit in-person key-handoff commitment.
